results.title: Construction of waste-to-resource knowledge graph for industrial ...
results.content: In this work, we propose an automated framework to construct a Waste-to-Resource Knowledge Graph (W2RKG) from pertinent research papers using Large Language Models, which enhances coverage, scalability, and standardisation of the resulting database. The discrepancies may stem from the following reasons: (1) some cases in Maestri are very specific, e.g., reusing a specific chemical material (e.g., silica, hydrochloric acid) or producing a specific product (e.g., coffin, tianium dioxide), which may not be included in the collected papers; (2) some cases in Maestri are rather straight-forward, e.g., reusing waste heat as heat resource, which typically are not specified in academic papers; (3) almost half of resources in Maestri are named as “raw material” without indicating the application or functionality of the resources, making the matching between Maestri and W2RKG challenging; and (4) Maestri contains IS case studies from diverse sources, whereas our W2RKG collects data from academic papers obtained from the Scopus Database, potentially missing valuable W2R knowledge in the real-world.

results.content: # [CfP] Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models (KG–LLM 2026) @ LREC 2026. Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models (KG–LLM 2026) @ LREC 2026. We are pleased to announce the Workshop on Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models (KG–LLM 2026), to be held in conjunction with LREC 2026 in Palma de Mallorca, Spain, May 16th 2026. We invite submissions of original research that leverages both Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) in any domain of Natural Language Processing or language resource development. Knowledge Graphs for Large Language Models. * Using linguistic or knowledge graphs as training data. All application domains are welcome (Digital Humanities, FinTech, Linguistics, Education, Cybersecurity, etc.) as long as the work uses both Knowledge Graphs and Large Language Models. * Language Resources: In line with LREC policies, authors are encouraged to describe, document, and share language resources, datasets, models, evaluation tools, or annotation guidelines used or created in their work. For questions, please contact the workshop organizers at: kg-l...@googlegroups.com.
